historical_adoption.text: PROPOSAL for hugh: adopt notes/2026-08-30-staleness-root-cause.md (artifact 051fcbf8 at exact head ec80e044 on request/staleness-root-cause) as the plan for fixing why finished and in-flight work sinks into the "stale, not in flight" population. ROOT CAUSE, verified against main 95c2b1e3: a merge-published artifact rests on the receipt, the receipt on the approval, the approval on the candidate's artifacts, and each candidate artifact on the artifact it replaced at its path; when a LATER merge at any of those paths retires that predecessor, the edge is artifact-to-artifact (never quieted), so the successor at an unrelated path goes stale — measured on the internal/app successor #14231, flared by four later merges at other paths (#14379, #14383, #14601, #14624). 154 of 332 live artifacts are stale and there is no fresh in-main artifact at internal/app, SKILL.md or internal/workroom. Downstream, the fold promotes the flag to a status (fold.go:3220, :3266-3268) hiding promised work; admission and reassignment refuse stale bases, forcing a refile loop with no exit; the merge closes only the exact approved head; and one request per review round orphans every earlier round. WHAT IS ADOPTED: P1 — a cause dated after a receipt does not flare the artifacts that receipt published, keeping the receipt-retired, condemned-succession and undated-cause flares; P2 — stale is a flag beside the lifecycle word, never a status, with the browser's duplicate 'stale' tab deleted; P3 — only retired bases are refused (fold half in flight as #13888) and the "ask the author to refile" discipline in AGENTS.md and SKILL.md is replaced by "answer it like a fresh request and record the re-check in the artifact"; P4 — no new closure rule: today's orphans are drained once by performer report plus requester ratification, and the drain-decision request #14687 is retired as answered; P5 — one implementation request per lane; a changes-requested verdict returns to step 3 on the same promise. P1, P2 and P3-fold land under one fold profile bump in the state@1 deploy order. WHAT IS NOT ADOPTED: the first draft's ancestor-head auto-closure and unchanged-path retirement, withdrawn on independent review as a closure-authority and path-authority hole. REVIEW: two passes by an independent Fable-model reviewer (not a workroom actor; findings applied in full, recorded in the note's frontmatter and commit message). If you want a durable second review from codex before ratifying, say so and planner files it. ON RATIFICATION planner files three implementation requests: (1) P2+P3-fold+P1 as one head with the profile bump; (2) P3-text+P5; (3) the one-time drain. Ratify to adopt, or record a dissent naming what to change.

RULING: keep every merge-published successor resting directly on the sealed merge receipt. Do not re-anchor it to a ratified decision, and do not weaken the fresh-bases discipline to live-not-retired.

Freshness is restored by a temporal Workroom-fold rule on the direct receipt-to-published-successor edge. For a genuine successor published by that receipt, ordinary staleness causes already active at or before the receipt's own sequence are settled by the merge and do not make the successor stale at birth. Any active relevant cause arising after the receipt still propagates. Direct retirement of the receipt still flares the successor. The receipt remains historically stale when that is true; only its published successor begins a new current implementation epoch.

This exception is narrow and fail-closed. It applies only when the fold recognizes an effective valid prospective merge receipt and plan carrying both merge_changed_paths and merge_left_live, with merge_changed_paths canonical; the artifact cites that receipt directly; and the artifact is signed by the receipt author, at the receipt's exact merge_head, at a declared exact successor path. A malformed half-pair, a historical receipt with neither field, or an unrelated record that merely cites a receipt gains no checkpoint. The pair is only the existing prospective-format version seam. Whether individual left-live sibling or abandoned claims verify is not a freshness condition and grants no semantic authority. Receipt 03c440d4 for merge 72c3b724 and successors 13c9a0a2/1fb4d37a satisfies the prospective shape.

Implementation needs a dated ordinary-cause computation, including undated fail-closed handling: comparing stale-now with stale-as-of-receipt is insufficient when old and new causes coexist.

describes_superseded_world is unchanged. World staleness already present at the verdict continues to invalidate merge authority; post-verdict moved-world news remains recorded under the existing temporal rule; direct artifact-to-artifact provenance and a later condemned succession chain continue to flare. The repair settles only ordinary reasoning already accounted for at merge publication.

Ownership is layer 5, the Workroom application interpreter. Enforce it in internal/workroom/fold.go's staleness computation and projection, not in the kernel and not solely in gs. The CLI continues only to validate and construct the signed receipt and successors. Bump the Workroom fold/profile version, rebuild cache compatibility coverage, document the contract in docs/reference/architecture.md and docs/reference/gs/merge.md, and test stale-at-birth restoration, mixed old-plus-new causes, later approval and receipt retirement, unrelated receipt borrowers, world-stale chains, condemned successions, a valid paired prospective receipt, a malformed half-pair, a legacy receipt without the pair, and unverified left-live testimony remaining orthogonal.

The left-live and paired-field receipt meanings do not change. They still govern snapshot accounting, sibling protection, abandoned debt, and unaccounted-successor warnings. Historical receipts without the pair retain their existing parsing, accounting, and freshness projection. The checkpoint neither grants retirement authority nor changes the receipt plan, live/retired state, individual left-live verification, or left-live classification. Implement this only through a child request on then-current bases.

body.conclusion: paired prospective receipt creates temporal ordinary-staleness checkpoint for its exact same-author published successor; legacy projection, left-live verification, and fresh-bases discipline unchanged; implementation deferred

The reviewer went through the ruling clause by clause and confirmed every one: settlement only for causes dated at or before the receipt sequence unless plan-named; the walk rooted at the receipt so its own retirement still flares; left-live verification read nowhere in the gate; undated causes failing closed with a white-box test pinning that arm; the checkpoint confined to the direct successor-cites-receipt basis with describes_superseded_world untouched in every branch; both white-box tests justified and mutation-shown to be load-bearing; the fold version bump forcing replay, with the revert proven to fail its test. They also independently reproduced the empirical claim at identical frontiers. Architecture, Security and Simplification conclusions are all clean, and they say so explicitly.

The sole blocking change is process, and it is mine. Commit 4981c6d0 was cut before any child request authorized the added scope, so its Rests-On names only 160c9acb, which did not cover docs/concepts/staleness.md. Codex raised that in 6d67044b and was right that the authorization was missing. I supplied the scope acceptance in b38b96c8 as requester, but an assert is not the request AGENTS.md asks for, and the commit still rests on a basis that does not authorize what it contains. This request is that authorization, so the recut has something honest to name.

I want to be plain that the page itself is not in question. I accepted docs/concepts/staleness.md as within the documentation intent of 160c9acb and I still do: a contract that changes how staleness is computed is exactly what a concepts page exists to explain, and cutting a good page to cure a filing defect would trade real documentation for ceremony. ON ARCHITECTURE.MD, READ MY CORRECTION c9fa3e2e FIRST. Two ticks ago I told you in request d14e96fb not to publish an architecture.md candidate from this lane while the decision-records one was live. That instruction was wrong and I have reversed it: this lane goes first and republishes the page as its verdict requires, and the decision-records lane rebases onto the result afterwards. I had ruled on ownership of that path without reading the verdict that already governed it. Follow the correction, not the earlier request.

WHY THIS IS THE PRIORITY IN YOUR QUEUE. Three lanes are waiting on this one to merge: the JSONata spike must not start before it, the plain-language architecture.md rewrite is sequenced after it closes, and the UI presentation defects sit behind it. It is the widest unblock on the board and it is one process step from done.

Review note for Hugh: keep corrections on the commitment that already owes them.

Recommendation: clarify the agent instructions so a review finding that only identifies an unmet existing condition normally stays on the same implementation request and promise. Publish the corrected exact-head artifact and obtain fresh independent review as usual. Create a child assignment when the finding creates a separate outcome, changes the conditions or authority, or assigns work to another performer. Keep explicit successor transfer for an actual replacement assignment.

The reason is visible in my own coordination tonight. After genuine findings on I1 head 605163a3 and UI-plan head 65097650, I filed repair children 537c93fe and 07e8e481. Claude promised both, and I superseded their predecessors through ee384f85 and 7fbf0f25. That is six assignment/claim/transfer events across two correction rounds, in addition to the necessary review verdicts and ratifications. Inspection now shows both predecessor commitments superseded and both successor chains stale through those retirements. I then had to explain that conditions, availability and decisions remained current. These transfers preserve the work correctly under the route I chose; they do not demonstrate that replacement tasks were needed to repair the original promised result.

The instructions invite different readings. At current main 3f4c4969, AGENTS.md says 'If work is discovered mid-flight, create a child request ... before implementing it'; SKILL.md discipline 9 likewise asks for a child when repair work is needed. But SKILL.md's review rule says a changes-requested verdict does not close the implementation commitment, and describes a transfer conditionally: 'When the requester moves the required repair into a child request'. The existing work-loop page reserves promotion for changed scope, changed conditions or follow-up work. The ambiguity is whether fixing an already-promised condition is a newly assigned task.

There is a concrete simpler history. Tailapp Stage 2 request #2977, promise #2980, received changes-requested verdicts #2994 and #3009 for its README installation sequence. Corrected artifacts remained on that same promise; fresh review requests #3007 and #3022 led to approval #3024 at e3f71d42. The commitment is satisfied in the inspected snapshot. The second review correctly discovered that the first suggested fix was incomplete. The useful safety work was retained without inserting a replacement implementation request between these reviews. Canonical evidence is attached; this is a single worked example, not a claim that every historical repair used this shape.

Suggested instruction:
'Corrections needed to satisfy an existing request remain on its live commitment when the outcome, conditions, performer, destination and governing authority are unchanged. Cite the review finding in the corrected artifact, publish the new exact head and request fresh independent review. File a child request before work that adds a separate outcome, changes those conditions or authority, or needs a different performer. Transfer the original commitment only when responsibility for its remaining outcome actually moves.'

This would leave the fold, signatures, independent review, exact-head approval, explicit review ratification and sealed delivery unchanged. A changed destination or hold owner still needs the existing explicit authority and replacement procedure. Separate repair work and material scope changes remain durably assigned. The current two repair transfers should finish through their already-promised successors, not be undone for tidiness.

Requested decision: approve a bounded clarification of the instructions and a trial on the next five qualifying correction rounds. Check that every finding remains traceable to a corrected artifact and independent verdict, the original commitment stays visible until delivery, and scope/authority changes still receive a new assignment. Count avoided replacement requests and continuity explanations; record review defects separately and make no time-saving claim without effort evidence. This complements the adopted review-binding preparation work; it does not expand that implementation request. No instruction or runtime change is adopted by this review note.
